extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ACL OCL corpus is derived from the ACL Anthology. We design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. Meta information is included, as the website's version is more accurate than that obtained by PDF extraction.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The ACL Anthology, which digitally archives all scientific papers in the CL domain, including metadata, PDF files, and supplementary materials.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The OCL corpus spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures, published from 1952 to September 2022.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We use GROBID for full-text extraction from PDF files. The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus can benefit existing research tasks as well as enable more opportunities, such as topic trend analysis, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, and pre-training scientific large language models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC, since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The corpus can be used for tasks such as topic trend analysis, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, and fine-tuning a general LLM.
